statement: A read that ends a change past its expiry is not a command: it moves an open change from the state it is in now, and when another caller moved the change first it answers the change as it is, the EXPIRED the other made or the state it was finished in, never a 409. A command still refuses an expired change (CTL-33). A change whose own revision is in effect is published, whatever its time: the read settles it PUBLISHED, as a retried publish does, and never records it EXPIRED while its revision decides; publishing a change recorded EXPIRED so, before this rule, settles it too (DR1-E-7).
guards: control:ExpiryRaceTest#two readers of a change that has just expired both read it expired
control:ExpiryRaceTest#a reader that lost the race to another terminal state answers the record as it is
control:ExpiryRaceTest#a change that moved to another open state meanwhile is expired from where it is
control:ExpiryRaceTest#a pass that listed the change before another reader expired it reads it expired
control:ExpiryRaceTest#a change that keeps changing under the read is a 409 after the attempts, never a guess
control:ExpiryRaceTest#a command still refuses an expired change with a 409 of its own
control:PublishedNotExpiredTest#a change whose own revision is in effect is settled published when its expiry comes, never expired
control:PublishedNotExpiredTest#a change no revision of which is in effect still expires
control:PublishedNotExpiredTest#a change recorded expired while its revision was in effect is settled by publishing it
